symptom: A pluggable widget with TWO datasources inside a data view (mxcli-demo-2's VoxelViewer) binds every unqualified attribute name to the LAST datasource's entity — the data view's own attribute (`rootPartNumber: IslandPartNumber` → `Bom.Part.IslandPartNumber`) and the attributes linked to the OTHER datasource (`childNumber` → `Bom.Part.ChildNumber`) alike. `check --references` passes, exec reports 'Created page', mx check reports CE1613 per attribute. Fully qualified names work
cause: Two passes, one shared slot. (1) The engine's explicit-key pass (widget_engine.go 4.6) re-applies every property authored by its schema key AFTER all datasource mappings, qualifying bare names with pageBuilder.entityContext — by then always the last datasource — so it overwrote the correctly-linked value the mapping pass had written. (2) entityContextFor fell back to that same slot for a property widget.xml links to NO datasource, which Studio Pro binds to the context object (the enclosing container), not to the widget's own data. check never asked which entity a widget attribute binds to at all
file: `mdl/executor/widget_attribute_scope.go` (resolveBindingScope + misboundAttributeError, shared), `widget_engine.go` (bindingScopeFor used by mapping pass, explicit-key pass and texttemplate params), `validate_widget_attribute_scope.go` (check --references)
insight: The binding rule is the widget's schema, not mapping order: DataSourceProperty set → that datasource; unset → the enclosing context (outerEntityContext, captured at Build start). A pass that runs after all datasources is where a 'current entity' slot is guaranteed wrong — look for every reader of pageBuilder.entityContext inside a multi-datasource Build. Reproduced end to end with a hand-built 5-file VoxelViewer .mpk dropped into a TestApp copy: pre-fix binary 2x CE1613 naming Bom.Part.*, fixed binary 0 errors; mx accepts a crafted mpk without CE0463, which makes a widget-shape repro cheap. check and exec share one refusal function, and a test asserts the exec error contains the check message verbatim. Trap: an ASSOCIATION property's entity is the one it LEADS TO (the option list), not its binding scope — routing it through the new rule gave CE8812 'does not lead to entity' on every association ComboBox; only the mx-check integration suite caught it, the unit suite was green
